Import data. 
Format categorical variables to be read by the table calculations.

```{r}
metadata <- read_excel("metadata/r_all_metadata_output.xlsx")


## Format categorical variables

# Location of participant
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    remoteness_group = case_when(
      remoteness %in% c("Major Cities of Australia", "Inner Regional Australia") ~ "Metropolitan and Inner Regional",
      remoteness %in% c("Outer Regional Australia", "Remote Australia", "Very Remote Australia") ~ "Outer Regional, Remote, and Very Remote"
    )
  )


# Income source
metadata$income_merged <- as.character(metadata$income_merged)


# Health Care Card
metadata$healthcare_card_cat <- as.character(metadata$healthcare_card)
metadata$healthcare_card_cat <- replace_na(metadata$healthcare_card_cat, "missing") #Replace NAs with categorical variable


# Last dental visit
metadata$last_dent_visit <- as.character(metadata$last_dent_visit)
metadata$last_dent_visit <- replace_na(metadata$last_dent_visit, "missing") #Replace NAs with categorical variable


# Usual reason for dental visits
metadata$dentist_reason_cat <- as.character(metadata$dentist_reason)
metadata$dentist_reason_cat <- replace_na(metadata$dentist_reason_cat, "missing") #Replace NAs with categorical variable


# Avoiding dentist because of cost
metadata$dentist_cost_cat <- as.character(metadata$dentist_cost)
metadata$dentist_cost_cat <- replace_na(metadata$dentist_cost_cat, "missing") #Replace NAs with categorical variable


# Study appointment setting at baseline
metadata %>%
  dplyr::distinct(location_baseline) #List appointment settings to recode (baseline)



# Baseline appointment locations
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    appt_location_b = case_when(
      location_baseline %in% c("ADL-SIM", "PAG-UOA", "CRF") ~ "University research clinic",
      location_baseline %in% c("PAG-HOME", "ADL-HOME", "ADL-H") ~ "Home",
      location_baseline %in% c("ADL-CC", "ADL-PT", "NCC", "ICP", "ADL-KY", "NREC") ~ "Community centre",
      location_baseline %in% c("HAW-M", "KANG", "QEH") ~ "Healthcare centre",
      location_baseline %in% c("NURI", "TAIK", "CBHS") ~ "School or childcare centre"
      )
    ) 


## Check output for baseline locations
metadata %>%
  dplyr::distinct(appt_location_b) #Check results



## Organisation recruitment variable
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    org_recruitment = if_else(
      is.na(community_organisation),
      "No",
      "Yes"
    )
  )
```


Recode variable for the table input.
```{r}
table_data <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    Gender = case_when(
      sex == "2" ~ "Female",
      sex == "1" ~ "Male",
      TRUE ~ "Missing"
    ),

    Age = case_when(
      adult_child == "adult" ~ "Adult",
      adult_child == "child" ~ "Child (under 18 years)",
      TRUE ~ "Missing"
    ),

    `Location of participant` = coalesce(
      as.character(remoteness_group), "Missing"
    ),
    
    `Income source` = case_when(
      adult_child == "child" ~ "Not applicable",
      adult_child == "adult" & is.na(income_merged) ~ "Missing",
      adult_child == "adult" ~ as.character(income_merged),
      TRUE ~ "Missing"
      ),

    `Health Care Card` = recode(
      healthcare_card_cat,
      "1" = "Yes",
      "2" = "No",
      "3" = "Unsure",
      "missing" = "Missing",
      .default = "Missing"
    ),

    `Time since last dental visit` = recode(
      last_dent_visit,
      "1" = "Less than a year ago",
      "2" = "More than a year ago",
      "missing" = "Missing",
      .default = "Missing"
    ),

    `Usual reason for dental visit` = recode(
      dentist_reason_cat,
      "1" = "Problem",
      "2" = "Check-up",
      "missing" = "Missing",
      .default = "Missing"
    ),

    `Avoided dentist due to cost` = recode(
      dentist_cost_cat,
      "1" = "Yes",
      "0" = "No",
      "missing" = "Missing",
      .default = "Missing"
    ),

    `Recruitment through organisation` = coalesce(
      as.character(org_recruitment), "Missing"
    ),

    `Study appointment setting at baseline` = coalesce(
      as.character(appt_location_b), "Missing"
    ),

    followup_status = case_when(
      as.character(followed_up) == "yes" ~ "Followed up",
      as.character(followed_up) == "no"  ~ "Lost to follow-up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


## Make a list of table variables
table_vars <- c(
  "Gender",
  "Age",
  "Location of participant",
  "Income source",
  "Health Care Card",
  "Time since last dental visit",
  "Usual reason for dental visit",
  "Avoided dentist due to cost",
  "Recruitment through organisation",
  "Study appointment setting at baseline"
)


## Convert the selected variables to long format
long_data <- table_data %>%
  select(followup_status, all_of(table_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(table_vars),
    names_to = "Characteristic",
    values_to = "Category"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !(Characteristic == "Income source" &
        Category == "Not applicable")
  )  # Remove child income data as it will be NA


## Count each category in the baseline cohort
baseline_counts <- long_data %>%
  count(Characteristic, Category, name = "baseline_n")


## Count follow-up outcomes within each baseline category
followup_counts <- long_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(followup_status)) %>%
  count(Characteristic, Category, followup_status, name = "n") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = followup_status,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )


## Combine counts and calculate percentages
table1 <- baseline_counts %>%
  left_join(
    followup_counts,
    by = c("Characteristic", "Category")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Followed up` = coalesce(`Followed up`, 0L),
    `Lost to follow-up` = coalesce(`Lost to follow-up`, 0L),

    baseline_pct = case_when(
      Characteristic == "Income source" ~
        100 * baseline_n / sum(metadata$adult_child == "adult",
                           na.rm = TRUE),
      TRUE ~
        100 * baseline_n / nrow(metadata)
      ),

    followed_pct = if_else(
      baseline_n > 0,
      100 * `Followed up` / baseline_n,
      NA_real_
    ),

    lost_pct = if_else(
      baseline_n > 0,
      100 * `Lost to follow-up` / baseline_n,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Baseline, n (%)` = sprintf(
      "%d (%.1f)", baseline_n, baseline_pct
    ),
    `Followed up, n (%)` = sprintf(
      "%d (%.1f)", `Followed up`, followed_pct
    ),
    `Lost to follow-up, n (%)` = sprintf(
      "%d (%.1f)", `Lost to follow-up`, lost_pct
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    Characteristic,
    Category,
    `Baseline, n (%)`,
    `Followed up, n (%)`,
    `Lost to follow-up, n (%)`
  )


## Print table output
table1
```

Statistical analysis.
```{r}
## As Fisher's simulated test changes slightly each time, set seed first to ensure reproducibility
set.seed(124)


## Define follow-up variable.
analysis_data <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    followup_binary = case_when(
      tolower(as.character(followed_up)) == "yes" ~ "Followed up",
      tolower(as.character(followed_up)) == "no"  ~ "Lost to follow-up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    followup_binary = factor(
      followup_binary,
      levels = c("Followed up", "Lost to follow-up")
    )
  )
 

## Check that counts match
table(analysis_data$followup_binary, useNA = "ifany")  # Yes correctly matching.



## Make categorical variables function
test_categorical <- function(data, variable) {

  test_data <- data %>%
    select(all_of(c(variable, "followup_binary"))) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[variable]]),
      !is.na(followup_binary)
    )

  tab <- table(
    test_data[[variable]],
    test_data$followup_binary
  )

  if (nrow(tab) < 2 || ncol(tab) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(
      variable = variable,
      test = NA_character_,
      p_value = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))

  if (any(chi$expected < 5)) {
    if (all(dim(tab) == c(2, 2))) {
      result <- fisher.test(tab)
      test_name <- "Fisher's exact"
    } else {
      result <- fisher.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE,
                            B = 10000)
      test_name <- "Fisher's exact (simulated)"
    }
  } else {
    result <- chi
    test_name <- "Chi-squared"
  }

  data.frame(
    variable = variable,
    test = test_name,
    p_value = result$p.value
  )
}
```



Run stats tests.
```{r}
variables_table1 <- c(
  "sex",
  "adult_child",
  "remoteness_group",
  "income_merged",
  "last_dent_visit",
  "dentist_reason_cat",
  "dentist_cost_cat",
  "org_recruitment",
  "appt_location_b"
  
)

results_table1 <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    variables_table1,
    function(v) test_categorical(analysis_data, v)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(p_value = signif(p_value, 3))


## Print results table
results_table1
```

Confidence intervals.
```{r}
## Categories to exclude from tests and per-category summaries
exclude_levels <- c("missing", "data missing", "retired/retirement savings") # Retirement category excluded due to small size (n = 4)

drop_excluded <- function(data, variable) {
  data %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[variable]]),
      !is.na(followup_binary),
      !tolower(as.character(.data[[variable]])) %in% exclude_levels
    )
}

test_categorical <- function(data, variable) {

  test_data <- data %>%
    select(all_of(c(variable, "followup_binary"))) %>%
    drop_excluded(variable) %>%
    droplevels()


  tab <- table(test_data[[variable]], test_data$followup_binary)

  if (nrow(tab) < 2 || ncol(tab) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(variable = variable, n = sum(tab), test = NA_character_,
                      p_value = NA_real_, cramers_v = NA_real_,
                      v_low = NA_real_, v_high = NA_real_,
                      OR = NA_real_, OR_low = NA_real_, OR_high = NA_real_))
  }

  chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))

  if (any(chi$expected < 5)) {
    if (all(dim(tab) == c(2, 2))) {
      result <- fisher.test(tab);                       test_name <- "Fisher's exact"
    } else {
      result <- fisher.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)
      test_name <- "Fisher's exact (simulated)"
    }
  } else {
    result <- chi;                                      test_name <- "Chi-squared"
  }

  # Cramér's V with two-sided 95% CI
  es <- as.data.frame(effectsize::cramers_v(tab, ci = 0.95,
                                            alternative = "two.sided"))

  # Odds ratio for 2x2 tables only
  or <- or_low <- or_high <- NA_real_
  if (all(dim(tab) == c(2, 2))) {
    f <- fisher.test(tab)
    or <- unname(f$estimate); or_low <- f$conf.int[1]; or_high <- f$conf.int[2]
  }

  data.frame(
    variable  = variable,
    n         = sum(tab),
    test      = test_name,
    p_value   = result$p.value,
    cramers_v = es[[1]],
    v_low     = es$CI_low,
    v_high    = es$CI_high,
    OR        = or, OR_low = or_low, OR_high = or_high
  )
}

## % lost to follow-up within each category, with exact 95% CIs
describe_categories <- function(data, variable) {
  data %>%
    drop_excluded(variable) %>%
    group_by(variable = variable, level = as.character(.data[[variable]])) %>%
    summarise(
      n        = n(),
      n_lost   = sum(followup_binary == "Lost to follow-up"),
      pct_lost = 100 * n_lost / n,
      ci_low   = 100 * binom.test(n_lost, n)$conf.int[1],
      ci_high  = 100 * binom.test(n_lost, n)$conf.int[2],
      .groups  = "drop"
    )
}

results_table1 <- bind_rows(lapply(variables_table1,
                                   function(v) test_categorical(analysis_data, v)))

categories_table1 <- bind_rows(lapply(variables_table1,
                                      function(v) describe_categories(analysis_data, v)))
```
